tess_devex: Quick note: observed missing request-id in logs when AsyncClient retries and when instrumentor is enabled. Tiny repro attached.

tess_devex: ```py
# repro: async client + retry + contextvar
from contextvars import ContextVar
from redwood import AsyncClient
ctx = ContextVar('req_id')
async def main():
    ctx.set('req-900')
    c = AsyncClient(retry_policy={'max_attempts':2})
    await c.generate_async('echo hi')
```

rahul_sdk: Thanks. Sounds like our retry/backoff creates child tasks without copying context. We should either centralise task creation with context.copy_context() or offer a hook.

mia_obs: Suggest a minimal typed API: register_observer(event: str, fn: ObsFn) where
```
class ObsFn(Protocol):
    def __call__(self, name: str, attrs: Mapping[str,str]) -> Optional[Awaitable[None]]: ...
```
This accepts sync or async callables. SDK can check if return is awaitable and await it.

rahul_sdk: That Protocol looks good. Implementation plan: 1) add ObsFn type + register_observer, 2) add internal _spawn_task(ctx, coro) helper that preserves context, 3) add small convenience bindings: bind_contextvar and instrument_opentelemetry.

tess_devex: Can we also include a sample-app integration test that asserts both logs and otel spans include req_id across retries? Would catch regressions.

infra-bot: created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-py/issues/803

rahul_sdk: I'll draft a PR with minimal changes to task spawning first and keep observer API for follow-up. Will include the sample app test.

tess_devex: Thanks 44d If helpful I can paste the failing logs into the PR description.
